content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to correct downward quickly.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not captured well.
- Lags in response to recent price drops — model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true price decline.
- Tends to overfit recent high volatility periods, leading to overconfidence in short-term momentum.
- Underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after major spikes — fails to account for “reversion to baseline” after peaks.
- Sensitive to initial conditions — forecasts are more accurate when starting from higher historical prices (e.g., 82–85 range) than from lower (e.g., 75–78 range).
